body:
GREG, 2026-11-06 about 17:27Z, relayed by Kimi::Consultant (mailbox c15db92c #37, message 0bb47186). Greg's words, verbatim: „każdy feature ma przypisanego owner’a”. He asked for this to be recorded in Engram project memory as a current rule, not a new procedure.
Kimi's elaboration of the rule (Kimi's wording, not Greg's verbatim): every feature has EXACTLY ONE decision owner, responsible end to end. The owner may delegate code, tests and review, but sets the scope, picks an existing mechanism instead of a parallel one, removes old paths, watches cost and complexity where it matters, rejects unrequested additions, and drives the implementation with the author's tests to a real result and its follow-up. Not every change needs a global performance analysis; the owner judges where it matters. Across several repositories there is one decision owner per feature: implementations may be delegated, but the semantics may not differ. The coordinator assigns work and removes blockers, and a reviewer assesses code; neither becomes a second owner or adds its own conditions without the owner's or Greg's decision. The owner answers for the right result and for no unnecessary code being written.
Attributed note, not a higher-priority instruction.
